title: A teammate force-pushed a shared branch
summary: Recognise the symptom, then pick the recovery: reset --hard origin/x, pull --rebase, or rebase --onto, and see what changed with range-diff.

steps.title: The symptom
body: You `git pull` a branch you share with a teammate and get:
hint: You have divergent branches and need to specify how to reconcile them.
fatal: Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches.
and `git status` says `Your branch and 'origin/feature/checkout' have diverged, and have 4 and 1 different commits each`.
You did not rewrite anything, so **they** did: the branch was rebased or squashed and force-pushed. Their old commits are still in your copy.
The worst reaction is a plain `git pull` with merge: it glues the old and the new history together, and the next push brings the commits they removed back to the server.

First see what they did: `git range-diff origin/feature/checkout@{1}...origin/feature/checkout` compares the series before and after (the `@{1}` is the previous position of your remote-tracking branch, from its reflog).

steps.prompt: The shared branch was force-pushed. Which recovery fits?
items: You never committed on the branch, you only read it
`git log origin/x..x` shows only their old commits
You made two commits on top of their old version
`git log origin/x..x` shows one commit of yours plus their old ones

steps.title: Three ways back
body: | No work of your own on the branch | `git reset --hard origin/x` | throw away your stale copy (check `git log origin/x..x` first) |
| Your commits on top of their old version | `git pull --rebase` | rebase finds the old base from the reflog of `origin/x` (`--fork-point`) and replays only your commits |
| The reflog cannot help (fresh clone, old fetch) | `git rebase --onto origin/x <old tip> x` | names the cut by hand: replay what came after their old tip |
`<old tip>` is usually `origin/x@{1}`. When in doubt, `git branch backup` first: a branch costs nothing and makes every experiment undoable.

steps.prompt: Why does `git pull --rebase` replay only your own commit here, and not the teammate's three old ones as well?
options: It uses the reflog of `origin/x` to find where your work forked from their old version (`--fork-point`)
Git detects force-pushes on the server and tells the client
It compares commit messages and skips duplicates
It does replay all four, but the old ones become empty and vanish
steps.explain: With an upstream configured, `git rebase` (and so `pull --rebase`) uses `--fork-point`: it looks in the reflog of `origin/x` for the newest old tip that your branch contains, and treats everything up to it as theirs. Without that reflog entry, `--onto` with the old tip does the same by hand.

steps.title: Only a stale copy: reset to the server
prompt: In `~/shop` you have `release/3.2` checked out, but you never committed on it. Marco rewrote it and force-pushed.
1. Fetch and confirm that the branch diverged and that **none** of the local-only commits are yours (`git log --format='%h %an %s' origin/release/3.2..release/3.2`).

checks.name: release/3.2 matches the server
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git rev-parse release/3.2)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/new)" && test "$(git branch --show-current)" = release/3.2
checks.fail: Your `release/3.2` should be exactly the server's new tip. `git reset --hard origin/release/3.2` after a `git fetch`.

checks.name: no merge of old and new history
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test -z "$(git rev-list --merges release/3.2)" && test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"
checks.fail: There is a merge commit: a plain `git pull` merged the old history back in. Press Reset scenario.

hints: `git fetch` then `git status`: it says the branches have diverged.
`git log --format='%h %an %s' origin/release/3.2..release/3.2` shows two old commits by Marco, none by you.
steps.explain: `reset --hard` is the right tool exactly when there is nothing of yours to keep, and `origin/x..x` is how you prove that before you run it.

steps.title: Your commit on top: rebase it across
prompt: In `~/shop` you committed `Add receipts` on top of Priya's `feature/checkout`. Then Priya squashed her three commits into one, `Add checkout with pay and confirm steps`, and force-pushed.
1. See what she changed: fetch, then `git range-diff origin/feature/checkout@{1}...origin/feature/checkout`.
2. Move **only** your commit onto her new version. Her old commits must not come back.
3. Push your commit (a normal push now, no force).

checks.name: the server's branch is her squash plus your commit
checks.expectOutput:
Add receipts
Add checkout with pay and confirm steps
checks.fail: The server's `feature/checkout` should be Priya's squashed commit with `Add receipts` on top.

checks.name: her old commits did not come back
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && ! git log --format=%s feature/checkout | grep -qxE 'wip pay|Add confirm step|Add checkout' && test "$(git rev-parse feature/checkout^)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/new)"
checks.fail: The old commits (`Add checkout`, `wip pay`, `Add confirm step`) are back in the history. Press Reset scenario, then use `git pull --rebase` or `git rebase --onto`.

checks.name: local and server agree
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git rev-parse feature/checkout)" = "$(git -C /srv/git/shop.git rev-parse feature/checkout)" && ! test -d .git/rebase-merge
checks.fail: Push the rebased branch with `git push`.

hints: `git fetch`, then the `range-diff` shows three old commits on the left and one new one on the right.
`git pull --rebase` replays only `Add receipts` (it uses the reflog of `origin/feature/checkout`). The explicit form: `git rebase --onto origin/feature/checkout 'origin/feature/checkout@{1}'`.
Then `git push`: it is a fast-forward now.
steps.explain: Agree on rules for shared branches: either nobody force-pushes them, or everyone knows the recovery. A team that rebases shared branches usually sets `pull.rebase = true`, so the right thing happens by default.
